    - You want to walk the trail or talk about walking it? I'd rather walk. Still, the rim's quiet for a moment. Say what you came to say, *Player*.
    - The Broken Ground to the far canyon bridge: the worst stretch, and you kept pace. Most of my own patrol can't. Don't tell them I said that.
    - Old Gnarl's down. The patrols can hold the ridges now, and the herds can go up. I'd have liked to swing the last blow myself, I admit it. I hate losing, even to a friend.
    - Imre's book of dates against Skarra's hide map: the shimmering nights fall right before the worst stirrings. I can't explain it. Nobody can. Ahvi has it now. Some things a chieftain carries without understanding.
    - Make it quick. The trail's waiting.

    - Tavi, chieftain of the Uskari. I left the rim young, trained a season with the swordsmen of the capital, and came home to hunt. When Hask became Old One, the Uskari chose me that same night. I doubled the patrols, and I still walk the worst stretch myself.
    - Skarra and I have been rivals since I came home, nineteen years now. Skarra's better with a map, I'm faster on a ledge, and we both say otherwise. That hide map with the red dots: Skarra shows it to me and nobody else.
    - Ketta trades away every patrol past one stretch of the canyon trail. Skarra lets it go without a word, so I do too. I know that kind of silence. I'll wait until Ketta is ready.
    - Ketta told me. All of it. I know that kind of silence from the inside, *Player*. So Ketta leads into that cave, not me. That's the only way out of it.
    - The canyon stretch is on our patrols again, and Ketta walks it every dawn. Ketta came to my fire last night just to complain about the cold. Best news I've had all year.
    - Howling Peak, then. Old Gnarl roots at the top, where the wind never stops. Watch the ground: the roots come up where it cracks. I'll open the way.
